classification.note: q95 is retained as a diagnostic but is not a LOW gate because sparse interictal-like events are part of the intended low state.

stage0b_post_canary_bracket.rationale: Stage 0 found I/I at q=0.820 and I/H at q=0.790 but no same-eta monostable anchors; add symmetric outer anchors without changing any classifier threshold.

stage0c_low_anchor_extension.rationale: The q=0.840 high-start arm scored 82.2 Hz and narrowly missed the frozen LOW median-rate limit of 80 Hz; extend once to q=0.860 without changing thresholds.

stage0d_q_only_coexistence_probe.rationale: The frozen q-only locator left q=0.825 on the low side when initialized low, but never tested a matched high initial state. Probe this single point before broad refinement because persistent LOW/HIGH separation would be the first strict empirical coexistence candidate.

stage0e_q_only_high_branch_bisection.rationale: At q=0.825 the low arm was LOW and the high arm decayed to INTERMEDIATE. Bisect toward the known q-only runaway side at q=0.800; run the high arm first and add the paired low arm only if a tonic-high branch survives.

stage0f_q_only_high_branch_bisection.rationale: The q=0.8125 high arm decayed to INTERMEDIATE, while the legacy q-only locator places the low-start escape interval between q=0.800 and q=0.825. Bisect q=0.80625 to test whether the high-branch survival and low-start escape boundaries separate into a narrow coexistence window.

stage1_adaptive_branch_edges.rationale: Stage 0 measured 6-35 minute wall times per 1.2-s arm and revealed a broad INTERMEDIATE band. The original 348-run rectangular grid is neither resource-proportionate nor the best discriminator. Locate high-branch survival and low-start escape edges separately, then spend the three-seed denominator only on any interval where LOW and TONIC_HIGH overlap.
stage1_adaptive_branch_edges.confirmation_trigger: Run full paired three-seed confirmation only at q values where the pilot low arm is LOW and the pilot high arm is TONIC_HIGH; extend INTERMEDIATE arms before treating them as an edge.
stage1_adaptive_branch_edges.claim_boundary: Adaptive allocation changes computational order only. It does not change the model, noise, classifiers, initial states, or three-seed robust-label rule.

claim_boundary: Finite stochastic SNN branch evidence only. A mathematical bifurcation label requires deterministic fixed-point continuation and Jacobian evidence; phase transition additionally requires a preregistered order parameter and finite-size scaling.
